title: Deferred egress smoothening and tenant-cohort sentry (hotfix)
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: During a transient regional egress saturation incident on 2026-02-17 we observed aggressive tenant-level circuit flips and abrupt global egress caps that caused long tail latency and tenant unfairness. This PR introduces two cooperating mitigations: 1) a deferred egress-smoothening algorithm that applies a short, topology-aware ramp to global egress caps instead of immediate hard clamps; and 2) a tenant-cohort sentry that groups noisy tenants into ephemeral cohorts and applies softer backpressure with a priority bias, preserving SLOs for unaffected tenants. Motivation: reduce oscillation and cascade restarts when SLO-budget-driven circuits trigger egress caps; reduce noisy-tenant blast radius; provide richer telemetry for post-incident diagnosis. This change is implemented as a targeted hotfix behind a feature flag (egress.smoothening_v2) and includes additional metrics, alerts, and a minimal change set to runtime admission and control-plane decision logic. The description below contains the full checklist, testing, and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] Implement deferred ramp algorithm in controlplane/egress (bounded ramp over 5s by default, configurable) - [x] Add tenant-cohort classifier and priority bias policy in runtime/circuit - [x] Emit new telemetry: egress.ramp_rate, tenant.cohort_id, cohort.backpressure_applied - [x] Unit & integration tests covering ramp boundaries and cohort demotion - [x] Canary rollout config and abort criteria in deploy/rollouts - [x] Add a golden end-to-end test in perf-canary harness - [x] Feature flag gating and config defaults tuned to conservative behavior Risk summary: The change touches decision logic for egress caps and request admission; to limit blast radius the flag is off by default and defaults are conservative (short ramp, low bias). If misconfigured, SLOs could still be impacted; additional runbooks and alerts are included. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind flag; 2) Canary in us-west with 2% of traffic for 30m; 3) If stable, increase to 20% for 2h while monitoring SLOs and ramp_rate distribution; 4) Gradual global rollout. Abort criteria: any sustained >1.5x tail latency on p99, or >5% increase in error rate for non-cohort tenants for >15m. Monitoring & alerts added: See telemetry section below. Related: Incident INC-3118 (support ticket SUP-4421), follow-up ENG-1960 for cohort tuning and long-term fairness work.
